file: The waste land(1922)Eliot Boni.djvu
title: The Waste Land (New York: Boni and Liveright, 1922): front cover
credit: Boni and Liveright, New York (publisher), 1922. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Page 1 of the same DjVu scan; the cover carries the notice of the Dial Award announced in December 1922.

file: The waste land(1922)Eliot Boni.djvu
title: The Waste Land (Boni and Liveright, 1922): title page with the Petronius epigraph
credit: Boni and Liveright, New York (publisher), 1922. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Page 9 of the Internet Archive scan (wasteland01elio, Duke University Libraries) of the first American edition, limited to 1,000 numbered copies, rendered from the DjVu on Commons. The epigraph: Nam Sibyllam quidem Cumis ego ipse oculis meis vidi in ampulla pendere (Petronius, Satyricon 48). Public domain in the US (published 1922); Commons tags PD-old-60-expired.

file: The Dial November 1922 vol. LXXIII No. 5.jpg
title: The Dial, vol. LXXIII no. 5, November 1922 (cover)
artist: The Dial Publishing Company, New York
credit: The Dial Publishing Company, New York, 1922. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: First American periodical printing of The Waste Land. Commons tag PD-US-expired. Original file is only 681 px wide.

file: THE CRITERION PORTADA.jpg
title: The Criterion, vol. 1 no. 1, October 1922 (cover)
credit: photograph by Commons user ANDMACRO, 2016. Licensed CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Photograph of the cover of the first issue of Eliot's quarterly, in which The Waste Land first appeared (16 October 1922). The photograph is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0; the 1922 cover itself is public domain in the US.

file: T.S. Eliot, 1923.JPG
title: T. S. Eliot, 1923
credit: Lady Ottoline Morrell, 1923. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Snapshot taken at Garsington, 1923; National Portrait Gallery, London (Ax141387 group). Commons tags: PD-old-80 (Morrell d. 1938) and PD-US-unpublished; the NPG asserts a claim over its reproduction, which Commons does not recognise.

file: Ezra Pound by Alvin Langdon Coburn, 1913, collotype photograph, from the National Portrait Gallery - NPG-NPG 78 14Pound-000001.jpg
title: Ezra Pound
credit: Alvin Langdon Coburn, 1913. CC0 1.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Collotype, National Portrait Gallery, London, released under CC0. Pound, 'il miglior fabbro', edited the drafts in Paris, January 1922.

file: Vivienne Haigh-Wood Eliot, seated, 1920.jpg
title: Vivienne Eliot (née Haigh-Wood), 1920
credit: Lady Ottoline Morrell, 1920. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Snapshot, National Portrait Gallery, London. Commons tag PD-old-80-expired. Original file 730 px wide.

file: From Ritual To Romance (Book Cover).jpg
title: Jessie L. Weston, From Ritual to Romance (Cambridge University Press, 1920): cover
credit: Cambridge University Press, 1920. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Scan from the Internet Archive; Commons tags PD-US-expired and PD-anon-70-EU. Original file only 388 px wide. Eliot's headnote: 'Not only the title, but the plan and a good deal of the incidental symbolism of the poem were suggested by Miss Jessie L. Weston's book on the Grail legend'.

file: RWS Tarot 12 Hanged Man.jpg
title: The Hanged Man (Rider–Waite–Smith tarot)
credit: Pamela Colman Smith, 1909. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Rider–Waite–Smith deck, first published by Rider & Son, December 1909. Madame Sosostris: 'I do not find / The Hanged Man' (l. 54-55); see Eliot's note on l. 46.

file: RWS Tarot 10 Wheel of Fortune.jpg
title: Wheel of Fortune (Rider–Waite–Smith tarot)
credit: Pamela Colman Smith, 1909. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Rider–Waite–Smith deck. 'Here is the Wheel' (l. 51).

file: Wands03.jpg
title: Three of Wands (Rider–Waite–Smith tarot)
credit: Pamela Colman Smith, 1909. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Rider–Waite–Smith deck. Eliot's note on l. 46 associates 'the man with three staves' with the Fisher King.

file: Michelangelo, sibille, cumana 01.jpg
title: The Cumaean Sibyl (Sistine Chapel ceiling)
credit: Michelangelo, c. 1510. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Fresco, Sistine Chapel, Vatican (Web Gallery of Art image; original file is 864 px wide). The epigraph from Petronius, Satyricon 48, concerns the Sibyl at Cumae.

file: Johann Heinrich Füssli 063.jpg
title: Tiresias Appears to Ulysses during the Sacrifice
credit: Henry Fuseli (Johann Heinrich Füssli), 1780–1785. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Watercolour, Albertina, Vienna (The Yorck Project image). Eliot's note on l. 218: 'Tiresias, although a mere spectator and not indeed a "character", is yet the most important personage in the poem'.

file: Gardner-Philomena and Procne.jpg
title: Philomela and Procne
credit: Elizabeth Jane Gardner Bouguereau, undated (before 1922). Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Oil on canvas (Art Renewal Center image). Cf. ll. 99-103 and Eliot's note citing Ovid, Metamorphoses VI.

file: Gustave Doré - Dante Alighieri - Inferno - Plate 9 (Canto III - Charon).jpg
title: Inferno, Canto III: the arrival of Charon
credit: Gustave Doré, 1861. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Wood engraving from Doré's illustrated Inferno (1861). The souls crowding the bank of Acheron: cf. Eliot's note on l. 63 ('I had not thought death had undone so many', Inf. III 55-57).

file: Inferno Canto 33 verses 62-63.jpg
title: Inferno, Canto XXXIII: Ugolino and his sons in the tower ('Then, not to make them sadder, I kept down my spirit in stillness')
credit: Gustave Doré, 1861 (this scan from an 1892 Cassell edition). Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Wood engraving (Project Gutenberg scan, 979 px wide). Eliot's note on l. 411 cites Inferno XXXIII 46: 'ed io sentii chiavar l'uscio di sotto all'orribile torre'.

file: 127.Ezekiel’s Vision of the Valley of Dry Bones.jpg
title: The Vision of the Valley of Dry Bones (Ezekiel 37)
credit: Gustave Doré, 1866. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: From La Sainte Bible (Tours, 1866), the 'Doré Bible'. Cf. l. 20 'Son of man' (Ezekiel 2:1) and 'dry bones' (ll. 390, Ezekiel 37).

file: 1602-3 Caravaggio,Supper at Emmaus National Gallery, London.jpg
title: Supper at Emmaus
credit: Caravaggio, 1601. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Oil on canvas, National Gallery, London. The journey to Emmaus (Luke 24) lies behind ll. 359-365 ('Who is the third who walks always beside you?'), per Eliot's note.

file: (Barcelona) The Golden Bough - Joseph Mallord William Turner - Tate Britain.jpg
title: The Golden Bough
credit: J. M. W. Turner, 1834. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Oil on canvas, Tate Britain. Photograph of the painting by Didier Descouens (PD-Art). Frazer's The Golden Bough takes its title and frontispiece from this painting (Aeneid VI).

file: James Abbot McNeill Whistler 006.jpg
title: Nocturne: Blue and Gold – Old Battersea Bridge
credit: James McNeill Whistler, c. 1872–1875. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Oil on canvas, Tate Britain. The Thames at night; cf. 'The river sweats / Oil and tar' (ll. 266-267). Image from The Yorck Project.

file: John Everett Millais - Ophelia - Google Art Project.jpg
title: Ophelia
credit: John Everett Millais, 1851–1852. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Oil on canvas, Tate Britain (Google Art Project scan). 'Good night, ladies, good night, sweet ladies' (l. 172) is Ophelia's exit line, Hamlet IV.v.

file: Sir Lawrence Alma-Tadema - The Meeting of Antony and Cleopatra.jpg
title: The Meeting of Antony and Cleopatra, 41 BC
credit: Lawrence Alma-Tadema, 1885. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Oil on panel, private collection (Sotheby's 2011). Note: the painting is dated 1885 on Commons, not 1883. Cf. 'The Chair she sat in, like a burnished throne' (l. 77) and Eliot's note citing Antony and Cleopatra II.ii.

file: Endurance trapped in pack ice.jpg
title: Endurance trapped in the pack ice of the Weddell Sea
credit: Frank Hurley, 1915. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: National Library of Australia (nla.obj-158918644). Commons tag PD-old-60-expired; published in Shackleton's South (1919) and Hurley's Argonauts of the South (1925), so also public domain in the US. Eliot's note on l. 360 refers to 'one of the Antarctic expeditions (I forget which, but I think one of Shackleton's)'.

file: Robert Havell after John James Audubon, Hermit Thrush, 1829, NGA 32199.jpg
title: Hermit Thrush (The Birds of America, plate 58)
artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
credit: Robert Havell after John James Audubon, 1829. CC0 1.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Hand-coloured engraving and aquatint, National Gallery of Art, Washington (CC0 open-access image). Eliot's note on l. 357: Turdus aonalaschkae pallasii, the hermit-thrush.

file: Hans Simon Holtzbecker, Hyacinthus orientalis almindelig hyacint ; Muscari comosum duskhyacint ; Brimeura amethystina pyrenæisk hyacint , , KKSgb2947-27, Statens Museum for Kunst.jpg
title: Hyacinthus orientalis, with Muscari and Brimeura (Gottorfer Codex)
credit: Hans Simon Holtzbecker, 1649–1659. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Gouache on parchment, Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen. 'You gave me hyacinths first a year ago; / They called me the hyacinth girl' (ll. 35-36).

file: The Botanical magazine, or, Flower-garden displayed (Plate 183) (8559498695).jpg
title: Syringa vulgaris, common lilac (Curtis's Botanical Magazine, plate 183)
credit: William Curtis, The Botanical Magazine, 1793. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Hand-coloured engraving, Biodiversity Heritage Library scan. 'April is the cruellest month, breeding / Lilacs out of the dead land' (ll. 1-2).

file: Dry Cracked Mud (4957b8b2-f52c-43b0-acc2-ead42cf6f03b).jpg
title: Dry cracked mud, Lake Mead National Recreation Area
credit: Andrew Cattoir, National Park Service, 2017. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: NPS photograph (NPGallery); work of the US federal government, public domain. 'Here is no water but only rock' (l. 331).

file: London Bridge, London LCCN2014693202.tif
title: London Bridge, London
credit: Bain News Service, c. 1910. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Glass negative, George Grantham Bain Collection, Library of Congress (LC-B2-2716-15). Crowds and horse traffic crossing London Bridge towards the City: 'A crowd flowed over London Bridge, so many' (l. 62). JPEG rendering of the LOC TIFF.

file: London Bridge LL Postcard.jpg
title: London Bridge, looking north to the City (LL postcard no. 74)
credit: Léon & Lévy (LL), Paris (publisher), postmarked 24 August 1910. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Postcard. Fishmongers' Hall is on the left; the steeple of St Magnus the Martyr and the Monument are on the right, at the foot of King William Street (ll. 62-68, 264).

file: John Woods - King William Street and St Mary Woolnoth - B1977.14.15668 - Yale Center for British Art.jpg
title: King William Street and St Mary Woolnoth
credit: John Woods (engraver), 1840. CC0 1.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Steel engraving, Yale Center for British Art, Paul Mellon Collection (B1977.14.15668), released CC0. Hawksmoor's church (1716-27): 'To where Saint Mary Woolnoth kept the hours / With a dead sound on the final stroke of nine' (ll. 67-68).

file: St Mary, Woolnoth (36640083551).jpg
title: St Mary Woolnoth, Lombard Street, City of London
credit: Amanda Slater, 2017. Licensed CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Flickr photograph, CC BY-SA 2.0; attribution required.

file: City of London , interior, St Magnus the Martyr - geograph.org.uk - 6863284.jpg
title: Interior of St Magnus the Martyr, Lower Thames Street
credit: Jim Osley, 2021. Licensed CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Geograph Britain and Ireland photograph, licensed CC BY-SA 2.0; attribution required. Wren's church: 'Inexplicable splendour of Ionian white and gold' (ll. 263-265) and Eliot's note.

file: The city terminus of the south-eastern railway. Wellcome L0028496.jpg
title: The City Terminus of the South-Eastern Railway, Cannon Street
artist: Lemon Hart Michael, for The Illustrated London News
credit: Lemon Hart Michael, for The Illustrated London News, 8 September 1866. Licensed CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Wood engraving, Wellcome Collection (L0028496), CC BY 4.0. The Cannon Street Hotel stood on the station's forecourt: 'To luncheon at the Cannon Street Hotel / Followed by a weekend at the Metropole' (ll. 213-214).

file: 1920 Bacon Pocket Map of London, England and Environs - Geographicus - London-bacon-1920.jpg
title: Bacon's New Map of London and Environs (pocket map)
credit: G. W. Bacon & Co., 1920. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Folding pocket map, courtesy Geographicus Rare Antique Maps. Covers Greater London from Amersham to Dartford; at 1280 px the centre is legible only in outline (Commons original is 5000 px).

file: Beach and ladies' bathing place, Margate, England-LCCN2002697068.jpg
title: The beach and ladies' bathing place, Margate
artist: Photochrom print, Photoglob Zürich / Detroit Publishing Co.
credit: Photochrom print, Photoglob Zürich / Detroit Publishing Co., c. 1890–1900. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Library of Congress, Photochrom Print Collection (LCCN 2002697068). 'On Margate Sands. / I can connect / Nothing with nothing' (ll. 300-302). Eliot convalesced at the Albemarle Hotel, Cliftonville, 22 October-12 November 1921.

file: Margate, Nayland Rock Shelter - geograph.org.uk - 6641255.jpg
title: Nayland Rock Shelter, Margate
credit: Christopher Hilton, 2019. Licensed CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Geograph photograph, CC BY-SA 2.0. The Grade II-listed promenade shelter where Eliot wrote part of 'The Fire Sermon' in October-November 1921 ('On Margate Sands. / I can connect / Nothing with nothing', ll. 300-302).

file: Margate, plaque commemorating T.S. Eliot at Nayland Rock Shelter - geograph.org.uk - 6641902.jpg
title: Plaque commemorating T. S. Eliot at the Nayland Rock Shelter, Margate
credit: Christopher Hilton, 2019. Licensed CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Geograph photograph, CC BY-SA 2.0.

file: Rottmanshohe from Starnberg, Upper Bavaria, Germany-LCCN2002696287.jpg
title: The Starnberger See: the Rottmannshöhe seen from Starnberg
artist: Photochrom print, Detroit Publishing Co. / Photoglob Zürich
credit: Photochrom print, Detroit Publishing Co. / Photoglob Zürich, c. 1890–1900. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Library of Congress, Photochrom Print Collection (LCCN 2002696287). 'Summer surprised us, coming over the Starnbergersee' (l. 8).

file: Berg (Starnberger See), Bayern - Salondampfer München bei Schloss Berg am Starnberger See (Zeno Ansichtskarten).jpg
title: The saloon steamer München off Schloss Berg, Starnberger See (postcard)
credit: Ottmar Zieher, Munich (publisher), c. 1900. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Postcard from zeno.org. Schloss Berg is where Ludwig II of Bavaria drowned in 1886, a story often linked to 'Death by Water'.

file: Munchen, Residenz vom Hofgarten aus. 703B (NBY 418775).jpg
title: Munich: the Residenz seen from the Hofgarten (Oilette postcard)
credit: Raphael Tuck & Sons, 'Oilette' series 703B, 1909. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Postcard, Curt Teich Postcard Archives (Newberry Library); Commons tag PD-US-expired. Original file is only 828 px wide. 'And went on in sunlight, into the Hofgarten' (l. 10).

file: Ouchy, from the Lake, Geneva Lake, Switzerland-LCCN2001702444.jpg
title: Ouchy (Lausanne) seen from Lake Geneva
artist: Photochrom print, Photoglob Zürich / Detroit Publishing Co.
credit: Photochrom print, Photoglob Zürich / Detroit Publishing Co., c. 1890–1900. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Library of Congress, Photochrom Print Collection (LCCN 2001702444). Eliot wrote much of the poem at Lausanne in November-December 1921: 'By the waters of Leman I sat down and wept' (l. 182).

file: Greenwich Hospital from the North Bank of the Thames RMG BHC1827.tiff
title: Greenwich Hospital from the North Bank of the Thames
credit: Canaletto, c. 1750–1752. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Oil on canvas, National Maritime Museum, Greenwich (BHC1827). JPEG rendering of the museum's TIFF. 'Greenwich reach / Past the Isle of Dogs' (ll. 275-276).

file: Richmond, view of the Thames, England-LCCN2002696955.jpg
title: Richmond: view of the Thames
artist: Photochrom print, Photoglob Zürich / Detroit Publishing Co.
credit: Photochrom print, Photoglob Zürich / Detroit Publishing Co., c. 1890–1900. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Library of Congress, Photochrom Print Collection (LCCN 2002696955). 'Richmond and Kew / Undid me' (ll. 293-294).

file: Sailing barges and a steamer, with a power station in the distance RMG PV1680.jpg
title: Sailing barges and a steamer, with a power station in the distance
credit: William Lionel Wyllie, c. 1900. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: National Maritime Museum, Greenwich (PV1680). Thames spritsail barges: 'The barges drift / With the turning tide / Red sails / Wide / To leeward' (ll. 268-272).

file: Robert Dudley Elizabeth Dancing.jpg
title: Queen Elizabeth I dancing la volta with Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester (traditional identification)
artist: unknown artist (French Valois school, formerly attributed to Marcus Gheeraerts)
credit: unknown artist (French Valois school, formerly attributed to Marcus Gheeraerts), c. 1580. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Oil on panel, Penshurst Place, Kent. Eliot's note on l. 279 quotes Bishop de Quadra's 1561 account of Elizabeth and Leicester on the royal barge ('Elizabeth and Leicester / Beating oars', ll. 279-280). Commons original is 1277 px wide.

file: DrapersTristanIsolde.jpg
title: Tristan and Isolde
credit: Herbert James Draper, 1901. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Oil on canvas. Eliot quotes Wagner's Tristan und Isolde at ll. 31-34 and l. 42 ('Oed' und leer das Meer').

file: Joseph Albert - Ludwig und Malwine Schnorr von Carolsfeld - Tristan und Isolde, 1865e.jpg
title: Ludwig and Malwine Schnorr von Carolsfeld as Tristan and Isolde, Munich premiere
credit: Joseph Albert, 1865. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Photograph of the first Tristan and Isolde, Munich, 10 June 1865 (Bayerische Schlösserverwaltung).

file: Siegfried and the Twilight of the Gods p 162.jpg
title: Siegfried and the Rhinemaidens (Götterdämmerung, Act III)
credit: Arthur Rackham, 1911. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Colour plate from Siegfried & The Twilight of the Gods (Heinemann, 1911). Eliot's note on l. 266: 'The Song of the (three) Thames-daughters begins here... V. Götterdämmerung, III, i: the Rhine-daughters'.

file: Rhinegold and the Valkyries p 072.jpg
title: 'The Rhine's fair children, bewailing their lost gold, weep' (Das Rheingold)
credit: Arthur Rackham, 1910. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Colour plate from The Rhinegold & The Valkyrie (Heinemann, 1910).

file: Preaching Buddha, Jamalgarhi, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, c. 200-300 AD, stone - British Museum - DSC01113.jpg
title: Preaching Buddha from Jamalgarhi, Gandhara, c. 200–300 AD
credit: photograph by Daderot, 2024. CC0 1.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Schist sculpture, British Museum (1895,1026.1). Photograph released CC0. 'The Fire Sermon' (Adittapariyaya Sutta) is the sermon Eliot's note on l. 308 calls a counterpart to the Sermon on the Mount.

file: New-York Mirror The Ruins of Carthage 1841.jpg
title: The Ruins of Carthage
artist: Alexander L. Dick after William Linton
credit: Alexander L. Dick after William Linton, 1841. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Steel engraving from the New-York Mirror, 2 January 1841. 'To Carthage then I came' (l. 307), from Augustine's Confessions III.

file: Quais de Smyrne (CNews) - btv1b53076942d.jpg
title: The quays of Smyrna (Izmir)
credit: Agence Rol (press photograph), 1922. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Bibliothèque nationale de France, Gallica (Rol 73108); Commons tags PD-France, PD-1996, PD-US-expired. 'Mr. Eugenides, the Smyrna merchant' (l. 209). Smyrna burned in September 1922, weeks before the poem was published.

file: Tibet Himalayas.jpg
title: Tibet. Himalayas
credit: Nicholas Roerich, 1933. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Tempera on canvas, Nicholas Roerich Museum, New York. Commons tag PD-old (Roerich d. 1947). 'Ganga was sunken, and the limp leaves / Waited for rain, while the black clouds / Gathered far distant, over Himavant' (ll. 395-397).

file: Gezicht op de rituele crematiestapels aan de Ghats van Benares en de Ganges Benares-Burning Ghats, Minarets of Arrangzebs Mosque (titel op object), RP-F-F02462.jpg
title: Benares: the burning ghats on the Ganges and the minarets of Aurangzeb's mosque
credit: unknown photographer (albumen print), c. 1850–1900. CC0 1.0, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (RP-F-F02462), released CC0.

file: Gottliche Komodie. T. 2, Das Fegefeuer 1871 (148975345).jpg
title: Purgatorio, Canto XXV: the souls in the refining fire ('E vidi spiriti per la fiamma andando')
date: 1868 (this page from the Berlin 1871 German edition)
credit: Gustave Doré, 1868 (this page from the Berlin 1871 German edition). Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
note: Full-page plate scanned by the National Library of Poland (Polona), including the page margins. The seventh terrace, where Arnaut Daniel 'hid himself in the fire that refines them' (Purgatorio XXVI 148, quoted at l. 427). Doré made no separate plate for Canto XXVI.
